Macht.et: From Middle High German maht, from Old High German maht. Cognate with Dutch macht, English might.

Machete.et: Borrowed from Spanish machete with a spelling pronunciation.

s: Er ist dieser Sprache nicht mächtig.

But what a disaster, it totally failed
Die Sahnetorte war mir zu mächtig.
The cream cake was too filling for my taste.
mächtig.et: From Middle High German mähtec (mähtic, mehtec, mehtic), from Old High German mahtīg, mahtīc, from Proto-West Germanic *mahtīg. Equivalent to Macht + -ig. Compare Dutch machtig, English mighty.

Macher.et: From Middle High German macher, from Old High German mahhāri. By surface analysis, machen (“to make”) + -er (agent suffix). Cognates include Dutch maker, English maker and, via Yiddish מאַכער (makher), English macher.

machiavellistisch.et: From the family name of the Italian philosopher Niccolò Machiavelli.
